MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p770/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the best form is the most upright creation, the return to the lowest is decrepit old age, and the reward of the faithful is undiminished.

MUJAHID:v2p770/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p770/r2.claim: The report says a believer who reaches decrepit old age continues to receive the reward of good deeds from youth and health; old-age actions do not harm him and sins after decrepitude are not recorded against him.

MUJAHID:v2p770/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p770/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p770/r3.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas adds that the believer is not held accountable for sins committed after returning to decrepit old age.

MUQATIL:95:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:95:1-6/r4.claim: Believers retain an undiminished reward without reproach: good deeds from youth and health continue to be recorded in old age and illness, but an unbeliever dies in shirk and faces Hell and God's anger.

FARRA:v3p276/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p276/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p276/r8.claim: Asfal sāfilīn means the Fire, with believers excepted; the generic singular “human” can refer to a group, as believers are excepted from loss.

MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p303#2/r4.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means not grudged; it may also mean not cut off.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p532#8/r3.claim: A believer who reaches old age retains the reward he had while able to work.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p533/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p533/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p533/r1.claim: Ghayru mamnūn means a reward that is not cut off.

TUSTARI:95:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:95:6/r1.claim: Believers who did good in youth continue to have the deeds of their youth recorded when weakness and old age prevent them from performing them.

TUSTARI:95:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:95:6/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:95:6/r2.claim: Their reward does not cease even when they can no longer perform the deeds.

TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p514/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that some people in the Prophet's time became senile; when asked about their lost understanding, God excused them and preserved the reward earned before their minds failed.

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r1.claim: Some interpreters treat the exception as connected to the generic singular ‘human’: it has collective meaning, like ‘humanity is in loss’ in 103:2, so believers may be excepted and a superlative may be related to a plural group.

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r2.claim: Ikrima says a person who recites the Quran is not returned to decrepit old age, and reads the phrase as senility so severe that one no longer knows after having known.

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r3.claim: Others say even believers may reach old age; the exception concerns those whose minds fail, whose deeds cease, and who can no longer add good, while their former good works continue to count.

TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p517/r4.claim: Al-Tabari allows a disconnected exception: even after being returned to the lowest state, believers who did righteous deeds retain their reward.

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a believer who becomes unable to continue a righteous practice in old age keeps receiving its reward until death.

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says obedience maintained throughout youth earns the same reward after the believer grows senile, without liability for acts committed after losing reason.

TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p519/r3.claim: Ibrahim says a believer who reaches decrepit age receives the reward of the best work he did in youth and health.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r1.claim: Ikrima says God pays the believer's reward or deed and does not hold him to account when old age returns him to weakness.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r2.claim: Ikrima says senility does not harm an elderly person if God ends his life upon the best deeds he used to do.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r3.claim: Qatadah says a person who reaches old age after doing good receives the same reward he had while able to work.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the descent as Hell and exempts believers from that fate; Mujahid glosses the exception as those who believe.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.claim: Hasan reads the exception after Hell as parallel to the exception of believers from loss in Surat al-Asr.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that people return to decrepit age, while believers who did righteous work in health and youth retain its reward in old age.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains an undiminished reward as one that is not reduced.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the reward as uncounted; Ibrahim gives the same interpretation.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r3.claim: Ibrahim also understands the reward as uncounted.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r4.claim: A further gloss is that the reward is not cut off.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers ‘not diminished,’ meaning their reward remains as it was in health and youth; he connects the word to manīn, something weak, and cites poetry to show the gift has no shortfall or error.

TAB-FULL:v24p522/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p522/r6.claim: The cited line uses the word ‘ولا’ to indicate that the gift contains neither deficiency nor error.

ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p343/r8.claim: Those who believe and act righteously are excluded from that decline.

ZAJJAJ:v5p344/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p344/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p344/r1.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means that no one reproaches them for the reward; another view means the reward is not cut off.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447#2/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the fig and olive as edible fruit, Sinai as the blessed Mount, and Mecca as the secure city; he reads best form as finest shape, the lowest state as Hell, and the believers' reward as uncounted.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3447/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas links the verse to people in the Prophet's time whose minds declined; God excused them and preserved the reward for their earlier good deeds.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449#2/r4.claim: Ikrimah says a believer returned to senility still receives the reward of health and youth, without being held to account for sins committed in that state or having the reward withheld.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3449/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says old age and weakness reduce a person's ability to work, but God grants the same reward as in youth.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p256/r11.claim: If the lowest state is Hell, believers are a direct exception from the plural pronoun in ‘We returned him’; if it is old age, they are a separate exception.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p256/r12.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted clause: a believer reduced to senility and confusion cannot perform worship, yet retains the reward of former practice.

NAHHAS:v5p256/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p256/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p256/r13.claim: He explains an undiminished reward as one that is not reduced.

THALABI:v10p240/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r3.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p240/r3.claim: A report from Anas says children’s good deeds benefit parents before puberty and sins are unrecorded; later, at extreme senility, the same good deeds as in health are recorded and sins omitted.

THALABI:v10p240/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p240/r8.claim: Believers whose minds and deeds cease in old age still receive the same record of good works they performed when young, healthy, and strong.

THALABI:v10p240/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p240/r9.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p240/r9.claim: He explains their reward as given without their having to perform the deeds then.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r28.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p300/r28.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses an undiminished reward as one not reduced; the source's list of additional explanations is cut off after introducing a poem.

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r14.claim: The reward promised to believers who do good will not be diminished.

QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p434/r15.claim: Another interpretation is that being returned to the lowest state means a state of misery and disbelief, from which believers are excepted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r1.claim: Believers who reach old age receive the reward for the good works they performed while healthy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r2.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r2.claim: Qatadah and al-Kalbi likewise say that one who reaches old age after good works receives the same reward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r3.claim: Ikrima says Quran recitation prevents decrepit old age and identifies the exception as the person who recited the Quran.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God credits an obedient believer in old age with the same deeds he performed in his youth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r5.claim: One explanation of an unending reward is that it is neither diminished nor cut off.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r6.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil explain that God continues the servant's good deeds without reminding him of the favor.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak calls it a reward without work.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers the first view: God preserves the reward of good works that old age prevents, neither stopping nor reducing it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r1.claim: On the Hell interpretation, believers are the exception and are not returned to Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p156/r2.claim: On the old-age interpretation, believers do not reach senility even if they live long; extended life does not make them decrepit.

WAHIDI-QT:95:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:95:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:95:6/r1.claim: A believer returned to extreme old age is credited with the same reward as when he worked, unlike an unbeliever; his reward is uninterrupted.

JISHUMI:v10p7469/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7469/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7469/r6.claim: Mann originally means cutting, as in al-manūn and al-maniyya because death cuts off life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r10.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r10.claim: In a report through Ikrima, Ibn Abbas interprets the exception as those who recited the Qur'an and says its reciter will not be returned to decrepit old age.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r11.claim: Ghayr mamnun means uncut or uninterrupted reward, since their former righteous deeds continue to be recorded for them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r12.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the promised reward as reward without having to perform deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r7.claim: Under the old-age interpretation, faculties and deeds cease, but believers who practiced righteousness keep receiving the record of deeds they used to perform after becoming feeble.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some people reached decrepit old age in the Prophet's time; the verse excused them and promised their earlier reward after their faculties were lost.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p472/r9.claim: Ikrima says old age does not harm a person whom God seals upon the best deeds he practiced.

KASHSHAF:95:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:95:6/r1.claim: The exception connects grammatically under the first interpretation of the preceding verse, but is disconnected under the second.

KASHSHAF:95:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:95:6/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:95:6/r2.claim: Righteous elderly people receive unending reward for obedience, patience through God's trial of aging, and worship despite weakened ability to rise.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p778/r13.claim: The exception is connected if the return means Hell's lowest ranks, but disconnected if it means old age; righteous elderly still receive unending reward for obedience and patience through frailty.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r11.claim: Even if believers undergo decline in this life, their afterlife reward is not diminished.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r15.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r15.claim: Mujahid and others explain mamnun as counted or measured, with reminders of the favor.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r16.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p500/r16.claim: Many commentators instead say mamnun means uncut off, from a word for a weakened or severed rope.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:95:4-6/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a Qurʾan reciter is not returned to decrepit old age, citing the verse.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:95:4-6/r7.claim: Believers and righteous workers are not returned to Hell; on the old-age reading, a believer is not reduced to senility.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
TABRISI:95:4-6/r8.claim: When an aged believer can no longer work, God continues recording the good deeds he used to perform.

TABRISI:95:4-6/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:4-6/r9.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:95:4-6/r9.claim: A believer who reaches decrepitude still receives the record of good deeds performed in youth.

TABRISI:95:6-8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:95:6-8/r1.claim: A report attributed to Anas says childhood good deeds benefit parents, age brings successive spiritual favors, and good deeds continue to be recorded in decrepitude.

TABRISI:95:6-8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:95:6-8/r2.claim: If authentic, the report means sins stop being recorded in extreme old age because reason and discernment have diminished.

TABRISI:95:6-8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:95:6-8/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:95:6-8/r3.claim: An unending reward can mean a reward that is not cut off; others explain it as undiminished, uncounted, or free of distress.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r1.claim: The exception follows because al-insān is a collective noun.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r2.claim: If verse 5 means old age, believers who recite the Qur'an are not returned to extreme old age.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r3.speaker: النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r3.claim: If old age makes a believer incapable of work, the deeds he used to perform are still credited to him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r4.claim: Even if old age prevents worship, believers are not deprived of reward because God knows they would continue good works if they retained their strength.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r5.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r5.claim: If verse 5 means the Fire, believers are excepted because they are not sent there.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p173/r6.claim: The meaning of mamnūn was explained at al-Qalam 68:3.

RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r1.claim: On the old-age interpretation, the exception is disconnected: faithful elderly people receive lasting reward for obedience and patient worship despite the hardships and weakness of aging.

RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r2.claim: On the Hell interpretation, the exception is connected to the preceding class.

RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r3.claim: An unending reward is either never diminished or cut off, or is given without reproach or reminding the recipient of favors.

RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p12#2/r4.claim: Both qualities suit divine reward: it must neither end nor be tainted by reproach.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers who reach old age retain recorded good deeds and erased sins, without being held accountable for deeds of their senility.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that when a worshipful person weakens in old age, God continues the reward for the prayers, fasting, and charity practiced in youth.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r3.claim: The Prophet says a servant who travels or falls ill receives the reward for the deeds he performed while settled and healthy.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r4.claim: Another interpretation says a believer who knows and acts on knowledge will not become senile, decrepit, or lose reason.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r5.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r5.claim: Ikrima says that one who recites the Qur'an will not be returned to decrepit old age.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r6.speaker: ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r6.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the prophetic blessing for a long life accompanied by good deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r7.claim: A report says God commands a deceased believer's two angels to worship at the grave until resurrection and records that worship for him.

QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:95:6/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says an uninterrupted reward is reward without further action; another explanation takes the phrase to mean reward that is not cut off.

BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:95:3-7/r4.claim: If the previous verse means old age, the exception is disconnected; believers who act righteously receive reward that never ends or is not reproached, and otherwise the ruling confirms the exception.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r1.claim: The fāʾ appears here though not in al-Inshiqāq, combining two accepted usages; under the first interpretation the exception is connected, under the second it is disconnected.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348/r2.claim: On the disconnected-exception reading, righteous elderly and chronically ill people receive unending reward for obedience and patience through old age, trials, and worship.

QASHANI:95:6-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:95:6-8/r1.claim: Believers let heart-light overcome ego-darkness and gain knowledge and practical virtues, rising to high ranks in the holy world.

QASHANI:95:6-8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:95:6-8/r2.claim: Their enduring reward is the gardens of hearts and selves, whose provision comes from the holy world and is free from corruption.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو العالية وابن زيد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn Zayd, and Qatada say the lowest state is Hell for disbelief, making the exception connected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p503/r13.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's elaboration excessive and begins to explain the continued reward of righteous people who reach old age.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r1.claim: Righteous elderly people receive unending reward for obedience and patience through the trial of old age.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r2.speaker: الرسول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r2.claim: Two reports say that a person reaching one hundred without new deeds is credited as in health, and that a believer reduced to decrepit age keeps the record of deeds from his strength.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p504/r3.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means an everlasting reward that is neither cut off nor begrudged to them.

SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r1.claim: The exception may be connected: people were lowered beneath the lowest in creation and form, referring to the people of Hell.

SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:95:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: after giving the human the best form, God lowers him through age and physical decline, while righteous elderly believers receive lasting reward.

IBNKATHIR:95:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:95:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:95:6/r1.claim: Their reward is unending and never cut off.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2#s095/r6.claim: Believers are the exception because God guides them through faith; they recognize the straight path, reflect, and remain steadfast in their confession that God is Lord.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.claim: Believers are the exception because God guides them through faith; they recognize the straight path, reflect, and remain steadfast in their confession that God is Lord.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.speaker: الأقليشي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r2.claim: Al-Aqlaishī says the body pulls the human downward: if intellect leads desire, a person ascends among the near; if desire leads, they descend to Hell and become remote.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r3.claim: The few believers are spared degradation because God preserves their insight and first disposition, strengthening their intellect and light as they age while weakening appetite.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r4.claim: Righteous deeds verify a claim to faith: they are beautiful words and acts rooted in belief, protected from desire and shaped by the prophetic way into justice and noble conduct.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p474/r5.claim: The passage uses omission by implication: the first clause omits sinful deeds, while the exception implies preserving humanity's original, sound form.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r1.claim: Believers receive a great, uninterrupted reward that is never reproached; when old age or illness stops their good works, they retain the reward they earned while healthy.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r2.claim: The reward reflects sincere resolve and continuing effort, yet its basis is ultimately God's favor; aged believers are credited with the good they did in health.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p475/r5.claim: The surah's oath recalls the Torah's account of God coming from Sinai, Seir, and Paran; ideal creation, the righteous, and the fallen summarize the Torah's beginnings, laws, and later history.

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r8.claim: An explicitly weak report identifies the Fig with Syria and Olive with Palestine, Sinai with Moses' mountain, and the secure town with Mecca; it allegorizes the human as Muhammad, the lowest as idolaters, and the exception as the four caliphs.

DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p553/r9.claim: He identified the Fig as Noah's mosque on al-Judi, Olive as Jerusalem, Sinai as its mosque, and the secure town as Mecca; return to the lowest means extreme old age, excusing contemporaries whose minds failed and preserving their prior reward.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r10.claim: He glossed finest stature as the most balanced form, return as extreme old age, and an unending reward as undiminished.

DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p555/r4.claim: He identified the first oaths as fruit, the blessed mountain, and Mecca; human creation is in the finest image, return is to Fire, believers are excepted, and their reward is uncounted.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r1.claim: When believers reach extreme old age, their earlier good deeds continue to be credited; age neither harms their former reward nor adds sins for later incapacity.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r2.claim: He glossed the finest form as the best image and the lowest state as Hell in the worst form.

DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p556/r3.claim: He identified the oaths with actual figs and olives, Sinai as the blessed mountain, and Mecca; finest form is youth and strength, senility is the lowest, and the believer retains reward without reproach.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r10.claim: The Prophet said the recording angel continues to credit good deeds when a person weakens and withholds bad deeds; a Quran reciter is spared senility and ignorance.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r4.claim: He said Quran reciters are not returned to decrepit old age, interpreting the exception as those who recite the Quran.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r5.claim: He reports a saying that Quran reciters avoid senility; linking it to 22:5, he says they do not reach the state of knowing nothing after knowledge.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r6.claim: He glossed the lowest as frailty without former strength and said Quran readers are not reduced to the state in 22:5; the exception refers to Quran's companions.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r7.claim: He said that when old age and weakness prevent work, a person still receives the reward of earlier youthful deeds.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r8.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r8.claim: The Prophet said that illness or travel earns the servant the reward of his usual good works; he recited the verse about an undiminished reward.

DURR-FULL:v8p557/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r9.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p557/r9.claim: The Prophet said an ill or traveling servant receives the reward of deeds normally done while healthy and at home.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says that whoever recites the Qur’an will not be returned to decrepit old age.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r11.claim: Their reward is in the fitting abode of honor; the connecting fa follows because “but” carries a conditional sense, or is causal on the first interpretation since they are rewarded in Paradise rather than changed into punishment.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r12.claim: Their reward is unending, in return for obedience and patience through old age, hardship, and worship performed despite weakness.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r13.claim: A report says a servant receives the reward of his usual deeds when illness or travel prevents him from doing them; the source applies this to old age as well.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r14.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r14.claim: A report in Abu al-Layth's tafsir says angels ask to worship in heaven after a believer dies; God sends them to his grave to record his good deeds until the Resurrection.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r15.claim: Another lexical possibility is that the reward is not something conferred as a favor or reproach, as explained at the end of Surat al-Inshiqaq.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r7.claim: The exception names those with sincere faith and the righteous deeds commanded and rewarded; grammatically it is connected to the collective sense of “We returned them,” or disconnected, meaning “but those who believed.”

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r8.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Layth says that one who knows and acts will not become senile or lose his reason.

BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p360#2/r9.claim: A hadith says blessed is the person whose life is long and whose deeds are good.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r1.claim: The connected exception refers back to humanity: believers will not be returned to the lowest state at resurrection, but will gain added beauty and radiance.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r10.claim: He gives a similar interpretation: a Qurʾān reciter will not reach the senility in which one no longer knows after knowledge.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r2.claim: Ghayr mamnūn may mean an uninterrupted reward, or a reward not reproached or held over its recipients.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r3.claim: If the exception is disconnected, the believers are a new subject and the sentence means, however, they receive reward; this answers the inference that equal aging entails equal outcomes.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r4.claim: He says whether an exception is connected depends on intended exclusion from the ruling, not simply inclusion in or exclusion from the group described.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r5.claim: Some restrict the believers to righteous elderly people, rewarded for patience when age prevents their usual worship.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r6.speaker: أبو موسى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r6.claim: A hadith says God records for the sick or traveling servant the reward of the deeds he did when healthy and resident; another version says the Prophet recited this verse.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r7.speaker: شداد بن أوس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r7.claim: A report says a believer who praises God during a trial rises cleansed like a newborn, and angels should record his prior healthy deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r8.claim: When a servant grows old and weak, he is credited with the reward of the deeds he used to do in youth.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r9.speaker: الحبر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p176/r9.claim: He says whoever recites the Qurʾān will not be returned to extreme old age; the author questions narrowing the believers to reciters and the claim that reciters avoid senility.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r1.claim: Believers who do righteous deeds in accord with God's pleasure are excepted: although bodily beauty may fade, they move toward salvation, absolute beauty, and a good final state.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.claim: The surah establishes human creation and religion, summarizes the preceding surahs, and prepares for the next; beginning the next surah with Read in your Lord's name is fitting because religion is true and God is the best judge.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r2.claim: Their reward is unending or free of obligation, continuing forever even when their bodies can no longer work and perish; they reach the culmination of the best form.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r3.claim: The oaths point to this rule: faith in the Creator, accountability, and righteous work for God lead to lasting reward, while those without faith and righteous deeds sink to the lowest state.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r4.claim: Religion is the law of accountability between God and people: humans submit in faith and good works, while God shows good and evil and applies reward and punishment; Islam contains both aspects.

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r5.claim: The ending of the previous surah, turn eagerly to your Lord, leads into the account of reward and punishment here.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r1.claim: Those who believe and act rightly preserve and perfect innate nature through faith and good deeds, reaching its intended completion in the afterlife with a lasting, uninterrupted reward.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r2.claim: Those who corrupt their nature keep descending until they reach Hell’s lowest depth, where their humanity is emptied out.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r3.claim: The two outcomes naturally follow the starting point: faith and righteous action complete sound nature toward bliss, while deviation and severance from the divine spirit lead to Hell.

QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:95:6/r4.claim: Faith is the means by which sound nature reaches its fullness, the cord joining it to its Creator, and the light showing its upward way; when cut, human nature descends to become fuel for Hell.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r10.claim: The surah praises the fine reward of people who follow Islam in its foundations and branches.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r4.claim: The surah presents Islam as humanity's sound primordial nature and treats departures from its foundations as corruption and misguidance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p419/r6.claim: The surah warns those who reject Islam.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p424/r6.claim: The exception for believers shows that faith is the fruit of rational constitution: it guides conduct and good treatment of people who share the truth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p427/r4.claim: People fall from their innate monotheism and reverent awareness by worshipping stones, animals, trees, time, or denying the Maker despite seeing creation and themselves.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r5.claim: The exception is connected to the general term “human”: nonbelievers remain low, while people who believe return from shirk to their original fitra.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r6.claim: Believers regain the original best constitution, and righteous deeds deepen the fitra and guide it toward additional virtues.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r7.claim: The conjunction of righteous works praises believers because faith motivates action; this describes the believers at the surah's revelation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p428/r8.claim: The exception cannot be detached from its general term because the fa in “for them is a reward” rules that reading out.

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the bodily-aging reading because it conflicts with the apparently connected exception: creation and aging apply generally to believers and unbelievers alike.

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r2.claim: Another view limits the human to the unbeliever and reads the return as casting him into Hell or reversing his bodily form, making the exception disconnected.

TABATABAI:95:6-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:6-8/r3.claim: The exception is connected to humankind, and the reward is unending; this consequence supports reading the return to the lowest as a return to misery and punishment.

TABATABAI:95:6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:95:6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:95:6/r1.claim: When a person believes what God taught and practices good, God raises him; Quranic parallels describe this ascent through faith and righteous deeds as an unending gift called a reward.

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed after surah 85, The Great Constellations.

ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:95:intro/r2.claim: It states a fundamental moral truth shared by all true religious teachings.

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: The formula for those who believe and do good works is characteristic of late Meccan and Medinan texts; the note refers to the literary-critical discussion of 103.

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Paret
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r2.claim: Paret translates the reward as one not later cited to beneficiaries as a favor, but as something owed to them by right.

CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:95:6:anmerkung/r3.claim: The author instead takes manna here to mean withhold or diminish, so the phrase promises reward that will not be withheld; Labīd's line supports this sense.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p372/r3.claim: The oaths validate the premise that God created humans in the finest form: those who honor innate guidance, accept the messengers, believe, and do right earn eternal reward, while those who reject it fall into ruin.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p373/r6.claim: The exception begins to identify the people whom God protects from disgrace: those who believe and do righteous deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r1.claim: Believers who honor their status as God’s best creation and do right are honored rather than humiliated, and receive eternal reward.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p374/r2.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means ceaseless and unending; the author rejects another interpretation as contrary to Arabic grammar.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r1.claim: At Sinai God aided an oppressed people for their patience, freed Israel from Pharaoh, and gave them a law that punished its enemies; this illustrates favor to the oppressed and punishment of wrongdoers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p377/r3.claim: Abraham’s faithfulness brought leadership after his greater sacrifice; God extended the promise only to descendants who follow him, excluding those who wrong themselves through disbelief or idolatry.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r2.claim: On that reading, verse 6 promises that older believers who did good deeds retain uninterrupted reward and spiritual progress despite bodily and mental decline.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:5/r4.claim: The commentary's preferred reading is that unbelievers who fail to do righteous deeds misuse their God-given potential and regress instead of developing and earning reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r10.claim: A hadith says that when a believer is returned to extreme old age, his deeds are recorded as they were during his strength.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r12.claim: Fī Ẓilāl al-Qurʾān focuses on spiritual capacities: rejecting faith reverses humanity's potential to rise above angels, making it fall below animals that follow their nature.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r13.claim: In this reading, believers preserve and complete their natural capacities through faith and good works, reaching their intended perfection.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.claim: The exception here requires faith and good works, whereas al-ʿAṣr adds mutual exhortation to truth and patience; that added practice prevents further loss of reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.claim: Al-Tibyān distinguishes duties one performs personally from the additional duty or merit of enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which can be individual, communal, or recommended.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.claim: Exhortation covers obligatory and recommended truth and patience; those who do it gain extra reward, while those who only meet personal duties lose that extra gain without being utterly ruined.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r20.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r20.speaker: مفسرون
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r20.claim: Ghayr mamnūn is explained either as undiminished or uninterrupted reward, or as reward unspoiled by reproachful reminders.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r21.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r21.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r21.claim: The author takes all senses of ghayr mamnūn as intended, describing reward that is lasting and free from reproach.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r22.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r22.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r22.claim: The added fa in fa-lahum gives the reward sentence a connection suited to this sura's context, unlike the parallel wording without fa in al-Inshiqāq.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r23.claim: Al-Inshiqāq spends many verses on disbelievers and their punishment but says little about believers, so omitting fa suits its concise reward statement.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.claim: Al-Inshiqāq begins with human toil and successive ordeals, whereas al-Tīn begins by honoring humanity; its fa therefore suits the emphasis on continuing, unclouded reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r9.speaker: مفسرون
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r9.claim: On the old-age interpretation, righteous elderly people continue receiving the reward they earned when healthy and strong.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#3/r12.claim: The verse endings were chosen to carry several meanings at once: al-amīn joins safety and trust, asfal sāfilīn old age and Hell, ghayr mamnūn lasting and unreproached reward, dīn religion and recompense, and aḥkam al-ḥākimīn wisdom and judgment.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r30.claim: The oath's answer fits the preceding places of revelation: it describes humanity's beginning in the best form and its eventual return to the lowest state.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r31.claim: People divide into those who accept the prophetic call and those who refuse it; most are returned low, while believers receive reward.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17/r32.claim: Because revelations provide a way of life for humans, the answer names human nature in verse 4 and the way of life in verse 6; a proper way must suit human nature.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.speaker: في ظلال القرآن
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r1.claim: The human spirit can rise beyond the angels when it follows its innate nature and faith, but can fall below every creature when it abandons them; believers preserve and perfect that nature.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p429/r2.claim: The verse accommodates the reported readings and also implies that unbelievers live in distress, as linked to the constricted life of 20:124 and the falling image in 22:31.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r1.claim: The Tin exception concerns deliverance from the depths of Hell, so faith and good works suffice; al-Asr concerns loss, where omitting mutual exhortation forfeits additional reward.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r2.claim: Someone who believes and acts righteously but does not exhort others loses reward he could have earned, without necessarily being among those brought to the lowest state.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r3.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p430/r3.claim: Al-Tibyan explains that al-Asr narrows its exception to include mutual exhortation, while al-Tin broadens its exception; exhortation adds to personal faith and good works, and its omission means loss without requiring descent to the lowest state.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r1.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r1.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong may be individually obligatory, communal, or recommended; mutual counsel covers obligatory and recommended truth and patience, earning reward beyond personal duty, so partial loss differs from total loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r2.claim: One reported meaning of “unfailing” reward is that it is neither diminished nor interrupted.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r3.claim: Another reported meaning is that the reward is not marred by reminding the recipients of the favor.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r4.claim: He accepts both senses: the reward neither ends nor is spoiled by reminders of favor.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p431/r5.claim: The wording ghayr mamnun gathers both senses, whereas “not cut off” or similar wording would convey only one.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p432/r1.claim: Tin adds fa before the reward because its context does not explicitly identify the people returned low, while al-Inshiqaq describes disbelievers at length and its believers briefly, making omission of fa suit that brevity.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p433/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqaq begins with human toil and successive hardships, whereas Tin begins by honoring humanity; this makes the added fa fit the affirmation that the reward continues without being marred.

STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:95:1/r4.claim: A further view makes the fig the Garden leaves Adam and Eve used to cover themselves and the olive the blessed tree; these may foreshadow human abasement and intellect's light.

STUDYQURAN:95:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r1.claim: The exception for believers makes it more likely that the preceding verse describes an inner spiritual fall.

STUDYQURAN:95:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r2.claim: An unceasing reward is never diminished or cut off in this life or the next.

STUDYQURAN:95:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r3.speaker: Āl and Q
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r3.claim: In this life, continued religious practice earns worship's reward even when illness prevents performance or travel requires shortened prayers or breaking the fast, as Islamic law permits.

STUDYQURAN:95:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:6/r4.claim: For the next life, the unceasing reward refers to Heaven's bounties.

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r1.claim: Al-Tīn is likely an early-middle Makkan sūrah revealed after Sūrah 85, though some consider it Madinan; it is named for the fig in verse 1.

STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:95:intro/r2.claim: Verses 4–6 describe humanity's exalted origin and fall when people fail to live by their true nature, a message like 103:2–3.
